reader_summary.overview: Today, we are breaking down Opendoor, and this is a unique episode. We recorded with Kaz Nejatian, the CEO of Opendoor, shortly after the company reported its first quarter 2026 earnings. The core of the conversation is how Kaz frames the company.

key_points.text: We recorded with Kaz Nejatian, the CEO of Opendoor, shortly after the company reported its first quarter 2026 earnings.
He argues that Opendoor is a market maker rather than a prop desk or an asset manager.
Buying lots of homes and selling them quickly gives Opendoor a live information advantage over the rest of the housing market that no other participant has.

 Introduction 
 Matt 
This is Matt Reustle, and today I have Kaz Nejatian, CEO of OpenDoor, fresh off the first quarter 2026 earnings release. We get into what is driving the strong execution quarter-to-quarter here. We've seen the product rollouts, the sales velocity, and the margin improvements that have Opendoor EBITDA positive as of April 1 , 2026 – and on track to be adjusted net income positive by the end of the year.

 Kaz is a fascinating CEO to watch, to follow, to listen to, and he does not disappoint. So please enjoy our conversation.

 Inside the Building 
 Matt 
I actually want to start bigger picture here. If you go back to February 2025, you are still at Shopify. You're ready to sell all of your possessions, lever up, and buy Opendoor. Take it private. You end up becoming the CEO in a much more traditional way.
